facts.label: Tabela de tarefas
facts.sub: Muitas famílias americanas colam na geladeira uma tabela com nomes, dias e tarefas. Quando alguém termina, coloca uma estrela ou um visto. É um jeito simples de dividir o trabalho.

facts.label: Mesada
facts.sub: A mesada é um dinheiro semanal que algumas crianças recebem. Em muitas casas, ela depende das tarefas feitas. É uma forma de ensinar os filhos a cuidar do próprio dinheiro.

pages.title: Jobs for the week · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a quiet Sunday evening in Columbus. Mia and her dad sit at the kitchen table. The house is messy after a busy week. There are dirty pots in the sink and towels on the floor. Her dad, Paul, has a big sheet of paper. He wants to make a chore chart for the family.
“Let’s make a chore chart for the week. What can you do?” says Paul. “I can mop the kitchen floor on Saturday.” says Mia. “Good. Who should rinse the dishes after dinner?” says Paul.

pages.title: Jobs for the week · 3/3
paragraphs: “That is fair. Can I put a star on the chart for each job?” says Mia. “Great idea! Here is a pen.” says Paul. Mia writes her jobs in small boxes. She will mop the floor on Saturday and rinse the dishes every night. Paul will scrub the pots, because Mia does not like it. Every job has a day, and every day has a name. Mia wants to tidy her room too, for a bigger reward. At the end of the week, she will get her allowance.
